drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's 'clawed by a wolf' restricted to a wolf, or does it set a threshold of predator size?
outcomeNote: A mishna lemma with a single amoraic ruling reported on it; no argument is joined in this unit.

segments.he: וּדְרוּסַת הַזְּאֵב. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בִּבְהֵמָה – מִן הַזְּאֵב וּלְמַעְלָה, וּבְעוֹפוֹת – מִן הַנֵּץ וּלְמַעְלָה.
segments.en: § The mishna states: «And» an animal that was «clawed by a wolf» is a tereifa. «Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says: In» the case of «an animal,» it is a tereifa if it was clawed by any predator «from the» size of a «wolf and upward. And with regard to birds,» they are tereifot if they were clawed by any predator «from the» size of «a hawk and upward.»
